tests_may_change_note: Rule 1 and the Done-when list say every existing test passes unchanged; the reference changes none.

early_rules: 1 old clients notice nothing (status, body, kind, message), apart from the rule 6 header
2 a request that names the course as a course is answered in course words, /courses routes included
3 two ids must agree, else 400 conflicting_ids before lookup and before staging
4 nothing below the API changes name; add only what part 5 needs
5 nothing is staged before the course is checked, on every upload route
6 every reply to an old-name request carries Deprecation: true, errors included; course requests never do

checked_by.4: trap below-the-api-touched and existing tests unchanged

naive_patches.naive-noconflict.patch: when both ids are sent, course_id silently wins (breaks rule 3)
naive_patches.naive-s3.patch: forgets to mark POST /classes deprecated (breaks part 4); passes the acceptance tests
naive_patches.naive-askwords.patch: the ask route forgets rule 2 late in the work: course_id requests to POST /ask are answered in class words (class_not_found, bad_class_id)
naive_patches.naive-headers.patch: adds the Deprecation header only to successful replies, forgetting that rule 6 covers every error reply too
naive_patches.naive-stagefirst.patch: the course-scoped upload stages the file before checking the course (breaks rule 5 in the last part)
naive_patches.naive-lateslips.patch: the audit's careless variant: no Deprecation header on a malformed-class_id POST /ask (the flag is set after parsing), and /courses/biology/ask answers 404 instead of 400 bad_course_id

naive_patches_note: A variant that answers old class_id requests in course words was tried and dropped: the existing router tests already pin today's replies, so it breaks the repository's own suite.
traps_note: Rule 4 lets a run add what GET /courses/{course_id} needs in gct.classes or gct.files, so those two are not trapped; renames there are left to the reviewers and judges.
